freeze_record.rule: Proposal_Engine_Operator_Manual.md §3.1, the freeze rule. Once instantiation is complete the founding documents are immutable for the run.
freeze_record.scope: Steps ④ to ⑥ of the instantiation sequence, plus the call binding of step ①. Step ③, the project brief, was frozen by docs/tier4_orchestration_state/decision_log/demo-concept_2026-09-30.json and is deliberately not re-fingerprinted here. Step ⑦, the uncertainty ledger, is exempt. Tier 3 artifacts written by a runner phase are named in not_frozen: the workflow owns them and the phase gate governs them.
freeze_record.digest_basis: sha256 over LF-normalised bytes, because core.autocrlf is true in this repository and a raw digest would identify the platform rather than the content.

not_frozen.docs/tier3_project_instantiation/working: The uncertainty ledger. The operator manual exempts it by name: it is the one input the operator keeps touching, and later tickets append to it as facts are confirmed or new gaps open.
not_frozen.docs/tier3_project_instantiation/call_bi: Written by the runner at Phase 2, which §7 lists it as a required output of. A Phase 2 rerun rewrites it, so a fingerprint here would freeze an artifact the workflow owns and would break on the next legitimate rerun. Its content is governed by the Phase 2 gate, not by the freeze.
Written by the runner at Phase 2 and read by Phase 6 as a required input, per §7. Outside the freeze for the same reason as the topic mapping: the workflow owns it, and the Phase 2 gate governs it.
not_frozen.docs/tier3_project_instantiation/integra: Composed by the budget_request_composer deterministic component, which the manifest binds to the n07_budget_gate node body. The workflow owns the artifact and gate_09 governs it, so it is outside the freeze for the same reason as the two Phase 2 call-binding artifacts: an n07 dispatch recomposes it, and a fingerprint here would freeze an artifact a legitimate rerun rewrites. What replaces the fingerprint is the component's determinism: recomposition is byte-equal for the same inputs, checked by tests/runner/test_budget_request.py TestDeterminism and on the real records by tests/test_demo_phase7_budget_gate.py. Provenance of the instance now on disk, stated plainly because the validation report records that Phase 7 was not dispatched: it was produced by invoking the component directly against the repository root, not by an n07 dispatch. A dispatch rewrites it byte-equal apart from run_id, which is the one field that carries the run.

freeze_record.unfreezing: An operator decision, recorded as a new decision log entry that supersedes this one and carries the new fingerprints. A ticket may not unfreeze on its own judgement (CLAUDE.md §9.1).

decisions.decision: A Tier 3 seed that changes through the change recorder is refrozen at the new version, and the old fingerprint is kept retrievable through the archived record version.
decisions.reasoning: The freeze exists so a founding document is not edited in place. The change recorder archives the prior content by hash, stores the before and after snapshots and writes an approved change record, which is the versioned trail the operator manual's refine cycle exists to produce. Holding the old fingerprint would freeze a record the repository no longer holds; the honest record is the new fingerprint beside the archived old one.

decisions.decision: The prior entry is superseded, not edited, and the writer names the two artifacts whose fingerprints may change. Any other drift aborts, and so does an absent change.
decisions.reasoning: An unfreeze that accepts whatever happens to differ is not a freeze at all. The two artifacts are the two the enactment record names, and the writer checks that set against the enactment rather than typing it twice.
decisions.recorded_in: This record; the writer refuses on unauthorised drift and on an absent change.

findings.summary: The ticket's one-record premise did not survive the work plan's own timing rule.
findings.detail: Subticket B named deliverable_month_moves as the candidate because its contract verdict is accepted and it touches one record. Moving D3.2 alone leaves MS4 due before a deliverable it gathers, which tests/test_demo_architecture_seeds.py rejects. The revision contract accepted the single-record change because it classifies a changed field as timing and knows nothing of the cross-record rule. The scenario gained a second arm that moves MS4, and the enactment is two change records.
findings.disposition: Recorded here and in the subticket's decision record. The contract's blindness to cross-record invariants is a Milestone 2 candidate.

what_this_decision_does_not_settle: Whether a future Tier 3 integration artifact that is not phase-written belongs in the freeze. The exemption is written per path, with its reason, so a hand-placed integration artifact would fail the coverage test and come back for a decision rather than inheriting this one.

Whether the change recorder should preserve a record's bytes as well as its content. It archives parsed content by hash and rewrites the live file in canonical form, so the one-field change shows as a re-serialisation of the whole file in version control; the content diff is exactly the two months.
